messages:
Alice S: Hey team — NimbusBank POC: they see ~1.2s TTFT on the hosted inference path (model: rwd-3b-v1). Customer wants sub-300ms for the demo tomorrow. Also asking if warmup/prefill increases costs. Can we swarm and list short mitigations?

Ben (sales): CC @Chris Infra @Dana SE — they need a quick recommendation + ballpark pricing impact. Customer timeline: demo tomorrow afternoon (ET).

Chris Infra: Thanks — quick asks: sample request payload (lengths), are you using streaming? any x-cache headers in responses? Is the POC on shared hosted or Dedicated?

Alice S: Sample payload pasted below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-3b-v1",
  "input": "Summarize the following policy... (approx 420 characters)",
  "max_tokens": 150,
  "stream": true
}
```
Also attaching the last 3 response headers we grabbed: ``x-cache: MISS``, ``x-instance-latency: 1.18s``, ``x-routing: hosted-us-east-1``

Chris Infra: Ok looks like cold prefix/cache misses + instance spin-up. Two quick troubleshooting steps: check the model variant (sometimes quantized variants have slightly longer first-token JITs) and verify client is not batching intentionally (batching for throughput can increase TTFT).

Chris Infra: Diagnostic commands: run the debug endpoint and paste logs:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/requests?since=10m&model=rwd-3b-v1"
```
Look for lines like: "cache MISS", "KERNEL_JIT: compile_time=...", "kv_cache_miss=true"

Alice S: Pasted a short log snippet we saw: 
```
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] request_id=abc123 x-cache=MISS kv_cache_miss=true KERNEL_JIT compile_time=340ms instance_spinup=720ms total=1.18s
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] request_id=abc123 routing=hosted-us-east-1 model=rwd-3b-v1
```

Dana SE: That log nails it — two contributors: kernel/JIT compile (~300-400ms) + instance cold spin (~700ms) + small KV cache prefill. Mitigations (fast):
- enable prefix caching / prefill (customer prompt prefixes kept in KV cache)
- send a tiny warmup request sequence 60–90s before the demo (5–10 short requests, 5–10 tokens each) to prime JIT + KV cache
- for immediate low TTFT during demos: use prefer_latency=true or an endpoint with reserved capacity (Dedicated) to avoid spin-up/batching delays

Dana SE: Example warmup curl (cheap tokens):
```bash
for i in {1..8}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-v1","input":"warmup","max_tokens":4}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 3;\
done
```
This will cost minimal tokens (~<50 tokens total) and typically brings TTFT down <300ms for the next minute or two.

Ben (sales): Great — can you confirm the pricing impact? Customer worried warmup will blow their credits.

Dana SE: Short answer: warmup is charged as normal per-request tokens. But with tiny 3–5 token warmup prompts, it’s negligible for a demo. If they need sustained low-latency in production, recommend Dedicated reserved capacity — that switches cost model to committed capacity (predictable monthly) and avoids per-request jitter. I can send a quick pricing note.

Chris Infra: Also check the client-side: some SDKs batch small concurrent requests into a single batched RPC for throughput. For demos set batch_window_ms=0 or prefer_latency=true so the runtime serves the request immediately rather than waiting to aggregate.

Alice S: Customer also ran the security questionnaire — they want SOC2, encryption at rest, and an IP allowlist for callbacks. Can we get the security pack + a light answers doc?

Dana SE: We have a canned security answers doc and a questionnaire PDF. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/security-pkg (internal link) — I’ll start filling in the NimbusBank section. @Ben (sales) can you share the completed customer questionnaire PDF?

Ben (sales): Uploading the customer's security form now (shared drive link): https://drive.company/nimbus-soc2-form.pdf

infra-bot: [infra-bot] Canary rollout for rwd-3b-v1 -> v1.1 completed in hosted-us-east-1 at 2026-03-20T13:50:00Z. No errors.

Chris Infra: Actionable checklist: 
- Dana: prepare warmup + pricing note (ETA: 2h)
- Alice: run the warmup commands against the customer's test key and confirm headers (x-cache: HIT) before the demo
- Ben: send security PDF to Dana and copy legal for IP allowlist

Alice S: Will run warmup now and report back in this thread.

Ben (sales): NimbusBank ok with a tiny warmup cost, wants us to automate warmup for the demo start. Can we add a one-off scheduled warmup job in the console?

Dana SE: Yes we can schedule a warmup task from Console -> Jobs -> Warmup; otherwise I can run a quick script from my laptop and hand them a curl snippet.

Alice S: Warmup done — headers now: ``x-cache: HIT`` and measured TTFT ~240ms on two requests. Customer happy.

Chris Infra: Nice. For follow-up: consider a small canary on Dedicated for Nimbus (30k/mo commit) if they want SLA and consistent <200ms TTFT at scale.

Ben (sales): Moving to next step with Nimbus procurement. Dana — plz attach the pricing blurb and security answers to the CRM.

Dana SE: Will do. Marking owner — Dana SE.

Alice S: Thanks team :thumbsup:
